text:
incident-bot: 🚨 [Pager] High GPU queue growth in gcp-sa-east1 (southamerica) — autoscaler failing to provision. current queued_requests=1243, avg_wait=48s, 5xx_rate=0.6% :rotating_light:
sam_w: I'm on it. Do we have an autoscaler error?
maya_r: seeing repeated quotaExceeded from GCP in the provisioner logs. grabbing logs now.
kevin_t: can we reroute traffic to us-east1 or brazil-south? latency implications though.
lina_ops: I can open a GCP ticket but SA-East1 is our secondary region for LATAM -- SLA impact note: some customers degrade.
cs-elaine: customer success, FYI — we're already seeing a CS alert about elevated error rates for a few enterprise customers. prepping comms.
incident-bot: Incident severity: P1-ish (service degradation). Paging oncall.
maya_r: logs snippet: ```ProvisionerError: quotaExceeded: Quota 'GPUS_ALL_REGIONS' exceeded. request_id=prov-84321
stack: provisioner.createNode -> cloud.apis.compute.instances.insert -> 403 Quota Error```
sam_w: autoscaler is repeatedly requesting more GPUs but GCP denies. Autoscaler retry loop: 5 attempts per minute. queue is backing up.
kevin_t: what's pool utilization?
maya_r: pool us-east1 free GPUs=18, sa-east1 free GPUs=0, warmPool=4 but warmpool GPUs are already claimed. Fairshare low-priority jobs are dominating claim window.
lina_ops: can we temporarily preempt low-priority workloads? set claim_threshold to 70% for 15m?
sam_w: yes we can evict low-priority; doing selective eviction now. runbook step: `scripts/evict_lowprio.sh --region=gcp-sa-east1 --pct=40`
kevin_t: starting redirect rule to send non-latency-critical inference to us-east1: `route.add --from=sa-east1 --to=us-east1 --selector='tier:best-effort'`
cs-elaine: please tag affected customers for outreach: customer_list from alert: [AcmeCorp, BrightDocs, Shopia].
infra-bot: quota advisory: there is a pending increase request in GCP console (req-98765) created 9m ago, status=under_review.
maya_r: autoscaler error details: ```ERROR autoscaler.manager - failed to create instance: googleapi: Error 403: Insufficient GPU quota 'GPUS_ALL_REGIONS' of type 'NVIDIA_T4' in project my-project. Requested 16, limit 32.```. We're bumping up against project-wide regional GPU caps.
sam_w: mitigation plan: 1) Evict low-priority jobs 2) Reroute best-effort traffic to us-east1 3) Start temporary downscale policy for batch jobs 4) Contact GCP quota team for emergency bump
kevin_t: executing traffic shift now. I'll monitor latencies.
lina_ops: I've emailed GCP support with high-priority flag, included metrics and customer impact. Also opened internal ATLAS ticket for quota governance.
cs-elaine: preparing status message for affected customers: short note about throttling and mitigation, ETA ~30-45m.
maya_r: note: some requests are hitting 429 from our gateway because queues exceed per-route limits -> increase route buffer causes more memory usage. maybe throttle upstream.
sam_w: applying temporary request rate-limit for non-auth customers: `gateway.update --route=/v1/generate --burst=200 --rate=50`
kevin_t: after reroute, initial observation: us-east1 CPU latency +12% but error rate drops for routed traffic. overall queue starts to shrink from 1243 -> 680 over 5m.
lina_ops: cross-check: any on-prem/private deployments impacted? No, only hosted in SA-East region.
incident-bot: @oncall-sam escalation timeline: 20m since first page.
sam_w: deploying eviction script now...```bash
./scripts/evict_lowprio.sh --region=gcp-sa-east1 --pct=40
# output: evicted 182 low-priority tasks, reclaimed 68 GPUs
```
maya_r: reclaimed GPUs appended to pool, autoscaler retried and succeeded for 4 nodes. provisioning lag ~80s per node.
kevin_t: good signal: queued_requests down to 290. 5xxs trending down.
cs-elaine: starting outbound to top-3 affected customers with the note and mitigation steps.
lina_ops: GCP support responded: asking for justification and urgent quota increase request in console. They asked for estimated sustained usage. I posted the telemetry link.
sam_w: temporary long-term plan: enable cross-region failover for hot routes and burst redistribution. For now, continue current mitigations.
kevin_t: can we enable model-scaling fallback? degrade to smaller model for non-critical requests?
maya_r: yes we can set model_alias fallback: `model.fallback:set --route=/v1/generate --to=redwood-small --pct=30`
cs-elaine: will note degraded quality in comms.
incident-bot: Pager resolved? Not yet.
lina_ops: update: GCP escalated request to quota team. They provisioned a temporary soft-allow of +24 GPUs for 1 hour pending review. That should relieve the immediate pressure.
sam_w: confirming: pool free GPUs now 28 after bump and evictions. Autoscaler drove us from warmpool to full nodes and queue is now at 72.
kevin_t: monitoring for churn. Reverting temporary rate-limits will be gradual.
cs-elaine: CS update sent; customers acknowledged and appreciate quick mitigation. No immediate churn.
maya_r: note to runbook: add step to detect global project GPU cap and escalate earlier. autoscaler only checked regional caps.
sam_w: action items: 1) Follow up with quota governance to request permanent quota increase for SA-East1 (+50 GPUs) 2) Add project-wide cap detection to monitor 3) Add automated cross-region reroute for burst > 60% for >5m 4) Post-mortem in #postmortems 5) Update public incident page if SLA hit confirmed
lina_ops: I'll own the short-term quota request and customer comms follow-up.
kevin_t: I'll own changes to routing+rate-limit heuristics.
maya_r: I'll add the cap-detection alert and adjust autoscaler to check project-level quotas.
cs-elaine: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> queue draining, error rate normalizing. Escalation remains open until permanent quota resolved.
sam_w: thanks team. keeping thread open for monitoring for 2h.
kevin_t: :thumbsup: any logs to attach for postmortem? I'll upload autoscaler traces and GCP quota responses.
maya_r: uploading snippets to the incident doc.
cs-elaine: ping me if we need customer escalations tomorrow.
incident-bot: closing page at 1715554412? (leave open)
